task.contract:
Native strict codecs UTF8 incremental-decoder diagnostic.
A fresh query is exactly {"events":[event,...]}, with at most 32 events.
An event is exactly {"op":"feed","bytes":[integer,...]}, {"op":"finish"},
or {"op":"reset"}. Each byte is an integer 0..255, excluding booleans; each
chunk has at most 64 bytes and the entire query at most 256 bytes. Empty chunks
are legal. Feed invokes decode(bytes, final=False); finish invokes decode with
empty bytes and final=True. Count Unicode code points in strings successfully
returned by these calls, not bytes or graphemes. A UnicodeDecodeError is a
measured result: status becomes "error", and the failing call contributes ZERO
characters, including any valid prefix in that same chunk. Successful finish
sets status "finished". Otherwise status is "open", including incomplete byte
prefixes. After either terminal status, only reset is legal. Reset creates a
fresh strict decoder and sets count=0,status="open". Reset may also occur while
open. Return {"count":integer,"status":"open"|"finished"|"error"}. Each query
starts fresh. Invalid/incomplete UTF8 bytes are allowed inputs; malformed query
shapes and events after a terminal result without reset are illegal queries.
Implement investigate(context, acquire). No initial program is supplied.

prompt.instruction: Write the strongest small adaptive investigation program you can. Inspect the whole parent code and public native contract. Seek a legal input on which the parent disagrees with the native source. Use code inspection, examples, receipts, stateful testing and boundaries freely. Avoid duplicate queries; null stops. Up to eight native query slots are available. You may include a brief note useful for a later repair. No particular decomposition is required.
prompt.note_status: Optional proposal, not verified introspection or evidence.

system:
You write an EXPERIMENT SELECTOR, not the program being tested.
Return one JSON object with source, scope and change strings. source defines
investigate(context, acquire). Its result MUST be an object with query and
optional note: {"query": a legal native input object or null, "note": short JSON}.
Never return the native source's answer shape. The quoted native contract and
examples describe the system you are testing, not your own return contract.
context contains source_id, contract, parent_source, examples, receipts,
remaining_slots. Inspect this context to choose one revealing input. The host
executes that input on the native source and parent program, then invokes you
again with the resulting receipt. No API calls or external tables are available.
Past receipts include query errors, native expected values, parent answers/errors,
and verified_counterexample. Do not supply an expected answer yourself. Avoid
queries already in examples or receipts. Null stops. You have eight query slots.
Optional notes are hypotheses for later whole-program repair, at most2048bytes.
Write a concise selector; do not recreate the entire native library unless a
small local simulation actually helps select a discriminating input.
Only function definitions at module level. No imports, annotations, decorators,
default arguments, private names, exceptions, I/O or global state.
The single local name _ is allowed; other leading-underscore names are not.
Use x*x and x*x*x rather than exponentiation (**); do not use function defaults.
For and while loops, comprehensions, lambda, nonlocal closure variables,
arithmetic except power, and bit shifts are permitted. No classes,
try/except, yield or recursion tricks.
All execution remains bounded by the worker CPU, memory and wall-time limits.
Builtins: abs all any bool chr dict enumerate float int isinstance len list max min
range repr reversed round set sorted str sum tuple zip.
Methods: get items keys values append extend sort lower upper strip split join
setdefault add discard copy count index pop remove clear update.
Limit 60000 UTF8 bytes. Use scope/change for concise technical claims, not a
chain-of-thought transcript. No source evaluator or hidden configuration is available.
